I farm only 4.1 mu, and there are just two people in my household, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation simple, steady, and low-risk. I have 35 years of experience and well irrigation, so I do not need to chase the most complicated approach. I will plant winter wheat on all 4.1 mu first, then summer maize on the same 4.1 mu after wheat harvest. For wheat, I will use improved seed because I want stable emergence, decent disease resistance, and reliable grain filling. I will put most of my effort into enough nitrogen, moderate phosphorus and potassium, and three irrigations, because in my conditions water and nitrogen decide yield. I will use rotary tillage for wheat because it fits my small area and is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing. After wheat harvest, I will sow hybrid maize on the whole field. For maize, I will save labor and moisture by using no-tillage after wheat, and I will keep fertilizer and irrigation at a moderate level because I want good ears without overspending. I will spray pesticides only when needed, but in my yearly plan I assume two applications for each crop to handle the usual weeds, insects, and disease pressure. My goal is not extreme yield; my goal is a stable harvest that matches my age, my labor, and my land size.
